It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while observing the “noise and tumult” of a world where rulers seek to "exalt themselves above the assembly of the LORD," and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the nature of idolatrous state power and the rise of tyrants in this hour? [13, 714, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who "malign" the truth and "demand things of God" that He has not granted them, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that the Master “sovereignly orders everything He has made”—including the rise and fall of "most formidable" empires? [4, 13, 20, 922, 1143, 1285, 1408, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find "diplomatic relations" with the culture, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the "vicissitudes of life" by exposing the "spirit of fraud" in every human kingdom [11, 28, 426, 1301, 1503, 1605, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the existence of an idolatrous ruler is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who "works all things according to the counsel of His will" (Ephesians 1:11) [15, 68, 223, 723, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Monument of Pride and the Usurper's Boast**

**Verse**
“The king spoke, saying, ‘Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for a royal dwelling by my mighty power and for the honor of my majesty?’ ” (Daniel 4:30). [789, 975, 1058, 1174, 1266, 1268, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals that tyrants consistently seek to “make a name for ourselves” through “building enterprises” designed to be “monuments to their pride” [702, 1233, 1288, 1315, 1431, Conversation History]. This “human pride” causes them to "defy God," as they “express their own hearts” and "think themselves much better than they really are" (Proverbs 18:2) [138, 324, 702, 1233, 1234, Conversation History]. When a ruler claims that he has built his kingdom by his own "mighty power," he is acting as a "spiritual swindler" who "disdains the Master" and "takes the name of the Lord in vain" [1, 22, 183, 236, 415, 1340, Conversation History]. Such rulers are "blind guides" who "practice lawlessness" (*anomia*) by living "as though He never gave a law to obey" (Matthew 7:23; 23:16) [213, 301, 501, 1058, 1396, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by the “showmanship” of human monuments or the "pompous words" of a "wicked ruler," for "the form of this world is passing away" (1 Corinthians 7:31; Daniel 7:11) [13, 91, 125, 1001, 1007, 1434, 1617, 1684, Conversation History]. Recognize that "your life is not your own," and you must "discipline your mind" to "submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake," yet never allow an earthly "monument of pride" to replace the "Rock of Ages" in your heart (1 Peter 2:13; 1 Corinthians 6:20) [12, 101, 116, 212, 702, 856, 952, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1670, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **theocratic context** of Israel, "national greatness" was often a "temporal sign" of God’s covenant blessing, yet the Jews were warned: “If you by any means forget the LORD your God... I testify against you this day that you shall surely perish” (Deuteronomy 8:19) [409, 726, 1353, 1519, 1546, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that the "true church" is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” whose "kingdom is not of this world," meaning we look for a "city whose builder and maker is God" (John 18:36; Hebrews 11:10) [13, 26, 36, 140, 142, 1313, 1426, 1529, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Heart of the Tyrant and the Divine Decree**

**Verse**
“ ‘For this purpose I have raised you up, that I may show My power in you, and that My name may be declared in all the earth’ ” (Exodus 9:16; Romans 9:17). [1315, 1324, 1330, 1331, 1353, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture teaches that the "LORD’s personal and direct involvement in the affairs of men" is so absolute that He "hardened the king’s heart" while simultaneously holding the king "personally responsible for his actions" [703, 1324, 1329, 1332, Conversation History]. God “harnesses the deeds of the wicked” to accomplish His “good and perfect ends,” proving that "nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan," even the "furious rage" of a "cruel and vicious blasphemer" like Nero (Isaiah 46:11) [5, 64, 79, 101, 1132, 1408, 1419, 1429, 1487, 1515, 1572, 1616, Conversation History]. Rulers who "neglect God’s righteousness" and "establish their own righteousness" unwittingly serve as "tools to accomplish His will," for “He raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” [15, 316, 723, 1407, 1487, 1532, 1533, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that “the Lord has established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all” (Psalm 103:19) [15, 18, 94, 201, 1143, 1408, 1515, 1532, 1572, Conversation History]. You must "discipline your body and bring it into subjection," refusing to let the “noise and tumult” of "savage wolves" frighten you, for "the Word of our God stands forever" while the "plans... of men vanish—like smoke they vanish away" (Isaiah 40:8; Psalm 102:3) [11, 20, 79, 116, 283, 1306, 1313, 1374, 1515, 1684, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, God used “hostile nations” as a "rod of My anger" to punish Israel’s "unfaithfulness" (Isaiah 10:5; 1 Chronicles 9:1) [717, 740, 924, 1110, 1130, 1316, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our "victory," teaching that even the “worst atrocity ever carried out”—the Cross—was subject to the “determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God,” ensuring that "the Word of God is not chained" even when His ministers are (Acts 2:23; 2 Timothy 2:9) [5, 25, 41, 121, 1132, 1283, 1420, 1431, 1487, 1504, 1567, 1646, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Despot and the Usurpation of the Temple**

**Verse**
“who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God or that is worshiped, so that he sits as God in the temple of God, showing himself that he is God” (2 Thessalonians 2:4). [759, 837, 882, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical pattern of rulers who claim divine authority culminates in the "lawless one" who "opposes and exalts himself," driven by a "rebellious heart" to "want the authority for himself" [880, 1505, 1506, Conversation History]. This "blasphemous arrogance" is described as "satanic," as it mimics the fall of Lucifer who said, "I will make myself like the Most High" (Isaiah 14:14) [116, 428, 833, 982, Conversation History]. Rulers who “turn the grace of our God into lewdness” and "deny the only Lord God" are “slaves of corruption” who "profess to know God, but in works they deny Him" (Titus 1:16; 2 Peter 2:19) [258, 306, 322, 614, 1381, 1396, 1407, 1415, 1441, 1468, 1496, 1501, 1507, 1508, 1551, 1572, Conversation History]. They use their "royal dwelling" as a "platform from which they look down on others," effectively "stealing the mind of Christ away from the body of Christ" [172, 281, 789, 975, 1233, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Never become so involved in this world” that you seek “deliverance” from a “despot” or a "media empire," for “no slave can serve two masters” (Luke 16:13) [51, 85, 98, 130, 145, 181, 259, 280, 1020, 1493, 1503, 1572, 1623, Conversation History]. Your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” by recognizing that "Jesus Christ alone is the head of the church," and we must “obey God rather than men” whenever a ruler tries to "tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel" (Acts 5:29) [101, 1144, 1176, 1300, 1316, 1406, 1431, 1525, 1527, 1529, 1636, 1637, 1638, 1670, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: From Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, "man-made representations" were an "abomination" because they attempted to "caricature" the Lord [708, 709, 725, 757, 1117, 1120, 1122, 1278, 1339, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the concept of authority, revealing that Christ's rule is “mediated... solely and only by His revealed truth,” and we find “repose of the soul” not in "political maneuvering and lobbying," but in the "finished work" of the Savior (John 19:30) [13, 16, 19, 24, 79, 134, 136, 142, 1144, 1313, 1316, 1445, 1515, 1519, 1529, 1646, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Weighing and the End of All Empires**

**Verse**
“ ‘God has numbered your kingdom and put an end to it.… You have been weighed on the scales and found deficient.… Your kingdom has been divided’ ” (Daniel 5:26–28). [37, 1061, 1402, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the "noise and tumult" of "tyrannical" regimes by fixating on the "consummation of history," where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 24, 31, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. "Earthly kingdoms go the way of all flesh," and even the "golden city" of the "oppressor" will "vanish—like smoke they vanish away" (Psalm 102:3; Isaiah 14:4) [11, 37, 63, 789, 976, 1460, 1684, Conversation History]. Because "the Father gave this supreme authority to His Son," the "church militant" is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” who wait for the Day when “the kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ” (Revelation 11:15) [13, 26, 30, 31, 360, 361, 380, 1132, 1143, 1199, 1313, 1426, 1445, 1503, 1524, 1525, 1636, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “perfect justice will come” and he will “wipe away every tear from their eyes” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Revelation 21:4) [14, 24, 94, 109, 201, 470, 816, 822, 948, 1033, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by resting upon the "surest foundation," for if God has "magnified Your word above all Your name," His "everlasting dominion" is "secure" (Psalm 138:2; Daniel 7:14) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 176, 201, 266, 278, 352, 412, 602, 614, 1132, 1143, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 303, 324, 332, 361, 405, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

The faith that sees the hand of God in the daily outworking of divine providence is not a lesser faith than the kind of belief that can only see God at work when He intervenes in some spectacular or supernatural or miraculous way. Which is the greater faith? Now God is free, of course, to work through ordinary means or extraordinary means, or supernatural means. But never is God uninvolved and shame on anyone for thinking that. Just because God's not doing miracles does not mean that He's remote or uninvolved. And furthermore, as we see in Scripture, miracles have a distinct purpose and by God's design they are extremely rare. It's not necessary to invent a miraculous explanation for every extraordinary turn of events in order to give God due credit for accomplishing His will in human affairs. He's always doing that. Miracles or no.

One of the dominant features of universal human fallenness is the sinner’s deception about his true condition. Motivated by pride, the depraved mind thinks itself much better than it really is. But God’s Word cuts through that deception like a sharp sword, diagnosing sinful men as incurably sick, rebellious by nature, and incapable of any spiritual good. As slaves to sin, all unbelievers are hostile toward God and unable to please Him in any respect.13 Their total inability is underscored by the fact that they are not just bound to sin; they are also blinded by sin and dead in it. They are “darkened in their understanding” (Eph. 4:18) and cannot comprehend spiritual truth because “the god of this world [Satan] has blinded the minds of the unbelieving so that they might not see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ” (2 Cor. 4:4).14 Furthermore, unbelievers are “dead in [their] trespasses and sins” (Eph. 2:1), “dead in [their] transgressions” (Col. 2:13), “dead even while [they live]” (1 Tim. 5:6). In the same way that a blind man cannot give himself sight or a dead man raise himself to life, so the sinner is totally unable to impart to himself either spiritual understanding or eternal life.
